opportunity: A function parameter the body only ever dereferences is declared as an integer, and whether it gets a pointer type depends on nothing but whether the first field the compiler reads sits at offset 0. Three lines of C under stock gcc -O2: `struct S { long pad; int a; int b; }; int sum(struct S *s) { return s->a + s->b; }` is `int sum(long a0) { return *(int *)(a0 + 8) + *(int *)(a0 + 0xc); }`, while moving `a` to offset 0 makes the same parameter `int *a0`. On coreutils fmt -O2 with `libctypes off` the same split shows on two neighbouring functions: put_word is `void sub_3000(unsigned long *a0)` and get_line is `void sub_3420(long a0, unsigned int a1)`, ground truth `FILE *` for both.

bisect.competing_call_vote_hypothesis: REFUTED -- the calls vote xunknown8, which is less specific than int8
bisect.conclusion: Both halves fail independently: the fold has no pointer candidate at all (TypeOpIntAdd::getInputLocal votes int8), and the up-edge that would supply one is refused. A candidate folded into build_localtypes is order-independent; flipping the up-edge would fire on every local and its pointee would be the access width, not the GT-dominant char *.

statements_folded_or_deleted.what_they_are: every one is a hoisted temp folded into its uses or a common subexpression recomputed at each use -- the value the vanished statement carried reappears in the statements that stay. Cited examples: O0 coreutils fmt sub_406b deletes `a1 -= *(int *)(a0 + 0x14);` and substitutes it into the two uses; O2 gzip sub_a870 turns one address temp into two recomputations inside one call; O2 gzip sub_9f80 deletes a loop-invariant bound and recomputes it in the loop; O2 tar sub_3b890 splits `*(uint4 *)(a0+0x18) | *(uint4 *)(a1+0x18)` into two temps and recomputes the `|` at both uses; O2 diffutils sub_9e40 deletes `a0 += v2;` and folds v2 into every subsequent index.
statements_folded_or_deleted.correction: the pre-review bundle claimed `statements_moved_or_deleted: 0`, which was false: the classifier's own STATEMENT bucket was non-zero and the O2-only sweep could not see the O0 cases at all.
statements_folded_or_deleted.classifier_note: the classifier's TYPES regex does not know `bool`, so a lone `bool vN;` declaration lands in its STATEMENT bucket; 1 byte hunk and 2 void hunks are that and are excluded from the counts above

benchmark.what_worse_0_does_and_does_not_mean: every binary in this corpus is gcc-built ELF from the coreutils family, and the shape this rule has to refuse is nearly absent from it. Measured over the 16-binary corpus sweep: exactly FOUR sites spell a named global subscripted by a parameter (`dat_24580[a2]` in O0 dash, `dat_9fcd0[a2]` twice in O0 tar, `dat_1f548[a2]` in O2 dash), and all four are byte-identical in all three arms. Every other `x[aN]` in the corpus is a pointer already typed as one. The guard ablation moves only 9 of 7,523 functions, none of them scored differently. So `worse 0` is a statement about gcc-built ELF coreutils-family code with almost none of the class in it, not about the rule in general; the class is pinned by a stage control instead, and the three-line gcc repro in analysis.md is what a reader should run against their own corpus before flipping anything.
benchmark.verdict: both arms are viable as OPT-IN tools: neither has a `worse` row, neither moves a function off perfect, and neither has a per-variable regression. `void` is the larger aggregate move (+32.87, 100 improved), `byte` wins five more perfect functions. This is NOT evidence for a default flip -- see default_flip below.

notes: Five defects were found by the measurements and fixed before shipping. (1) The rule typed the x86-64 FS_OFFSET segment base, which is a function input but not a parameter, and that stopped `stackguard` recognising the canary on coreutils ls sub_d820 -- fixed by FuncProto::possible_input_param. (2) Not following PTRADD/PTRSUB made the candidate oscillate against the pointer-arithmetic rewrite and run the seven-pass settle ceiling. (3) Overriding a vote that is already a pointer replaced `free`'s correct `void *` with `undefined1 *` and was the entire `worse` column of the first typesweep. (4) [review] An INT_ADD whose constant addend was itself a global object address forwarded the walk, so a parameter indexing a byte table was typed `char *` and the named global was replaced in the body by its raw address. (5) [review] The first fix for (4) refused on the pointer bound alone, which cost nine correct bzFile * declarations in bzip2; it now grades the constant instead.
preset_decision: default `void` (docs/features/ptrfromuse/default-on-evaluation.md); multi-valued, so outside aggressive_carries_every_default_off_option, and in no preset: the default applies under every mode

rule.candidate: a pointer of the default data space's address size (eight bytes on the 64-bit images the option is named for, four on a 32-bit image), pointing at one unknown byte (`byte`, renders `char *`) or at void (`void`)
rule.considered: function INPUT varnodes only, and only storage FuncProto::possible_input_param accepts, and not type-locked
rule.walk: breadth-first over the transitive descendants through COPY/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT identity, the base slot of PTRADD/PTRSUB, and INT_ADD with a literal; visited set, ten-hop cap; accepts when a terminal use is the address operand of a LOAD or STORE. Breadth first so the cap is a property of the graph (everything within ten hops of the input is seen) rather than of the traversal order -- depth first recorded whichever path reached a shared Varnode first, so whether a refusing use just past the boundary was classified depended on pop order. Measured: the switch types one more function in the 16-binary corpus (O2 tar sub_3c8f0) and leaves the typesweep bit-identical in both arms.
rule.refuses: INT_MULT, INT_DIV/SDIV/REM/SREM, INT_2COMP/INT_NEGATE, any shift, PIECE, any float opcode, a comparison against a non-zero literal, a CALL whose callee prototype committed that argument to a non-pointer, and an INT_ADD whose constant addend resolves to a global object
rule.neutral: an INT_ADD with a variable addend, and an INT_ADD whose constant addend is address-like but names nothing
rule.fold: offered to get_local_type's fold by Datatype::type_order, never as a replacement seed, so libctypes' FILE * (SUB_PTR_STRUCT) and DWARF both outrank it; it also never speaks when the fold already has a pointer

constant_addend_grades.why: `p->field` and `table[i]` lower to the same INT_ADD of a value and a constant; only the constant says which operand is the base. The test is ActionConstantPtr::isPointer's own: the default data space's pointer bounds, resolve_constant into that space, then the global scope.
constant_addend_grades.Object (a global symbol at the resolved: REFUSE -- the constant is the base, so the walked value is a subscript
constant_addend_grades.Maybe (address-like, names nothing): NEUTRAL -- same as a variable addend. A stripped image's .bss table looks like this, and so does a genuinely large struct (bzip2's 0x13f0-byte bzFile, read at +0x1394 and +0x13e8)
constant_addend_grades.No (below the space's pointer lower boun: the walk carries on; an ordinary field offset
constant_addend_grades.residual_exposure: a parameter used ONLY to subscript an unnamed table is declined (nothing gives it a base); a parameter used both as such a subscript and as a real memory base is typed on the strength of the second use
constant_addend_grades.measured_cost_of_the_refusal: guard ablation: rebuilt with the constant test short-circuited and re-ran the byte arm over the same 16 binaries. 9 of 7,523 functions differ, all in bzip2 (bzFile *, fields at +0x1394/+0x13e8). With the flat 'at or above the bound => refuse' rule all 9 were lost; with the three grades 1 is recovered (O0 bzip2 sub_b9c1, which also dereferences its parameter at an ordinary offset) and 8 are still declined. The typesweep is bit-identical either way, so the refusal costs nothing the metric can see.
constant_addend_grades.controls: tests/stages/kuna-ptrfromuse.xml `globalindex` (Object arm) and `blindindex` (Maybe arm); each proven two-pass with a throwaway build that short-circuits its arm

default_flip.recommendation: none. The earlier bundle recommended flipping `void` on; that recommendation is withdrawn.
default_flip.why: the evidence attached to it is one corpus -- gcc-built ELF, coreutils family, PIE -- which contains zero instances of the shape the rule has to get right, and a decompiler option that commits a parameter to a pointer is a claim about every binary, not about this corpus. A flip PR would need, on top of the usual 0/675 + stages + speed evidence: a corpus with byte-element global tables (firmware LUTs, character-class tables, string tables), at least one non-gcc toolchain, and a non-ELF container.
default_flip.what_stands: both arms are safe to reach for by hand, which is what change_kind opt-in-tool means.
